column2: In which Vālmīki asks Nārada for the perfect man, and Nārada names Rāma, previewing his exile, battles, victory, and reign
In which Vālmīki, grieving a slain krauñca at Tamasā, curses the Niṣāda in verse and gains Brahmā charge to sing Rāma.
In which Vālmīki, seated on sacred grass, envisions Rāma's entire destiny from wedding and exile to Laṅkā's fall and triumphant return.
In which Vālmīki trains Kuśa and Lava to sing his Rāmāyaṇa, sages weep and reward them, and Rāma brings them to his palace to hear their song.
In which the Ikṣvāku Rāmāyaṇa is promised, and rich Kōsala, Manu-built Ayōdhyā, and Daśaratha ruling like Indra appear
In which truthful Daśaratha guards prosperous Ayōdhyā where contented citizens, dutiful varṇas, and mighty war hosts keep dharma secure
In which King Daśaratha, served by eight loyal ministers and priests Vasiṣṭha and Vāmadēva, rules a peaceful and righteous kingdom without rivals.
In which sonless Daśaratha vows a horse sacrifice while Sumantra recalls Sanatkumāra foretelling R̥ṣyaśr̥ṅga bringing rain and royal sons
In which Lōmapāda's courtesans enter the forest, charm innocent R̥ṣyaśr̥ṅga with songs and sweets, and lead him to rain-blessed Aṅga
In which Daśaratha heeds Sanatkumāra prophecy, visits Lōmapāda, and escorts R̥ṣyaśr̥ṅga and Śāntā to celebrating Ayōdhyā
In which Daśaratha, longing for sons in spring, propitiates R̥śyaśr̥ṅga, summons Vedic priests, and orders horse release and Sarayū ground prepared
In which Daśaratha seeks offspring rite from Vasiṣṭha, who orders lodges, feasts, honors all castes, summons Janaka and every king, and opens sacrifice
In which Daśaratha performs flawless horse sacrifice on Sarayū, feasts all guests, rewards priests, and wins promise of four sons
In which R̥śyaśr̥ṅga begins offspring rite while gods plead with Brahmā against Rāvaṇa and pray Viṣṇu be born as Daśaratha's four sons
In which Viṣṇu agrees to slay Rāvaṇa in human form, choosing Daśaratha, whose rite yields divine payasa for three queens
In which Brahmā commands gods to beget shapeshifting monkey sons who swarm earth to kill Rāvaṇa beside Rāma
In which Daśaratha welcomes four newborn princes, plans their marriages, and honors sage Viśvāmitra, pledging to grant his every wish
In which Viśvāmitra seeks boy Rāma for ten nights to guard his vow from flesh-blood raining demons, stunning Daśaratha with fear
In which Daśaratha, stunned, withholds boy Rāma as unfit for war, offers himself and his army, and hears of Rāvaṇa and his agents Mārīca and Subāhu
In which Viśvāmitra rages at Daśaratha breaking promise, earth trembles, and Vasiṣṭha praises his weapons to urge sending Rāma
In which Daśaratha gives Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa to Viśvāmitra, who amid flowers and drums leads them to Sarayū and grants Balā and Atibalā
In which Viśvāmitra wakes Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa at dawn, shows the river meeting and Kāma āśrama, tells how Śiva burned Kāma, and rests overnight
In which Viśvāmitra ferries Rāma across Gaṅgā, explains roaring Sarayū waters and fallen Malada and Karūṣa, and orders him to kill Tāṭakā
In which Viśvāmitra tells how Tāṭakā won elephant strength by boon, fell to Agastya curse, and must die by Rāma hand
In which Rāma, bound by paternal command, answers Viśvāmitra, fells Tāṭakā with one arrow, winning gods praise before night camp.
In which Viśvāmitra, pleased after the night, grants Rāma every celestial weapon with its mantra, and the living arms offer service.
In which Rāma learns withdrawal lore from Viśvāmitra, dismisses embodied weapons to mental service, and asks whose deer-filled hermitage grove lies ahead
In which Viśvāmitra tells of dwarf Vāmana outstepping Bali, then brings Rāma to Siddhāśrama to guard his rite from demons
In which Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa guard Viśvāmitra six sleepless nights, Rāma ocean-hurls Mārīca, slays Subāhu, and wins Siddhāśrama praise
In which sages invite Rāma to Janaka sacrifice to see the god-given bow none can string and journey to the Śōṇā where Rāma asks about the land
In which Viśvāmitra traces Kuśa sons founding four cities and tells how Vāyu cripples Kuśanābha hundred daughters for refusing him till their father questions them
In which Kuśanābha honors his daughters' forgiveness, brings Brahmadatta son of Cūlin, and weds them all as his touch straightens their limbs.
In which Viśvāmitra traces his line from Kuśa to Gādhi, tells how Satyavatī becomes the Kauśikī river, and rests at midnight
In which Viśvāmitra leads Rāma from the Śōṇa to the Gaṅgā bank and tells how Himavat's daughter Gaṅgā goes to the gods and Umā to Rudra
In which Rāma asks why Gaṅgā takes three paths, and Viśvāmitra tells of Śiva restrained, Kārtikēya born of fire, and Umā cursing heaven barren
In which Brahmā sends gods to Agni and Gaṅgā, whose burning embryo yields gold and six-faced Skanda, nursed by Kr̥ttikās, conquering Daityas and anointed commander.
In which Bhr̥gu grants Sagara sixty thousand sons and one heir, cruel Asamañja drowns children and suffers exile, and Sagara resolves on sacrifice
In which Viśvāmitra tells Rāma how Indra steals Sagara's horse and sixty thousand sons dig earth to Rasātala till gods appeal to Brahmā
In which Brahmā foretells doom, Sagara sons honor four world elephants, accuse Kapila of stealing the horse, and burn to ashes at his Huṃkāra
In which Aṃśumān questions direction-elephants, mourns ash-heaped fathers, learns from Garuḍa Gaṅgā alone frees them, returns horse, and Sagara completes sacrifice and dies
In which Bhagīratha earns Brahmā's grace through fierce penance and learns only Śiva can bear Gaṅgā's descent to save Sagara's sons
In which Śiva traps sky-falling Gaṅgā in his locks for years, then frees her to follow Bhagīratha earthward amid rejoicing gods
In which Brahmā frees sixty thousand Sagaras as Gaṅgā floods their ashes, names her Bhāgīrathī, and Bhagīratha returns to rule joyfully
In which Rāma crosses Gaṅgā to splendid Viśālā and hears Viśvāmitra tell ocean churning, Vāruṇī choice, and Indra triumph
In which grieving Diti wins from Kāśyapa boon for Indra-slaying son, then serving Indra splits her impure-sleeping womb sevenfold while Indra begs forgiveness
In which Indra makes Diti's forty-nine sons the Maruts, Viśvāmitra traces Viśālā's line to Sumati, and Sumati welcomes travelers
In which Sumati feasts Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, Rāma questions empty hermitage near Mithilā, and Viśvāmitra tells Gautama curse on Indra and Ahalyā awaiting Rāma
In which gods give gelded Indra ram testicles, Rāma frees radiant Ahalyā, Gautama reunites with her, and Rāma departs for Mithilā
In which Janaka welcomes Viśvāmitra to his sacrifice, marvels at Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, and learns their lineage and deeds
In which Śatānanda questions Viśvāmitra about Ahalyā reunion with Gautama, welcomes Rāma, and begins telling Viśvāmitra royal lineage and march to Vasiṣṭha hermitage
In which Vasiṣṭha welcomes Viśvāmitra, exchanges welfare questions, presses a feast on his reluctant guest, and summons Śabalā to cook it
In which Śabalā feasts Viśvāmitra's army at Vasiṣṭha's command, and Vasiṣṭha refuses riches untold rather than yield his wish-granting cow
In which dragged Śabalā flees to Vasiṣṭha, proves brāhmaṇa might beats Kṣatriya, spawns Pahlava and Śaka-Yavana hosts, and Viśvāmitra answers with missiles
In which Śabalā's foreign hosts rout Viśvāmitra's army, Vasiṣṭha burns his hundred sons, and Śiva-armed Viśvāmitra torches the grove as Vasiṣṭha lifts his staff
In which Vasiṣṭha swallows Viśvāmitra's blazing arsenal and Brahmāstra with one Brahmadaṇḍa, driving humbled Viśvāmitra to seek brāhmaṇhood through tapas
In which Brahmā hails Viśvāmitra rājar̥ṣi after thousand-year tapas, the shamed sage resumes fiercer austerities, and rejected Triśaṅku begs Vasiṣṭha sons for bodily heaven
In which Vasiṣṭha sons curse defiant Triśaṅku into caṇḍāla form, and the deserted king begs Viśvāmitra for bodily ascent to heaven
In which Viśvāmitra shelters caṇḍāla-born Triśaṅku, calls sages to his heaven rite, and curses Vasiṣṭha scoffers to outcast births
In which Viśvāmitra sends Triśaṅku bodily heavenward, stops his fall from Indra and creates southern stars for his headlong refuge
In which Viśvāmitra shifts austerities to Puṣkara while Ambarīṣa buys willing Śunaḥśēpa after Indra steals his victim
In which Viśvāmitra curses his refusing sons, arms Śunaḥśēpa with two hymns, and Indra grants the bound boy long life at Ambarīṣa's rite
In which Mēnakā's beauty steals ten years of Viśvāmitra's tapas until remorse sends him to Kauśikī for Maharṣi rank while Indra summons Rambhā
In which Indra sends Rambhā to tempt Viśvāmitra, who curses her to stone for ten thousand years and repents his anger
In which Viśvāmitra conquers anger in thousand-year silent tapas, Brahmā grants Brahmanhood, Vasiṣṭha befriends him and Janaka welcomes the fulfilled sage
In which Janaka tells the deposit of Rudra bow, Sītā rise from the furrow, routed besiegers, and his vow to wed her to Rāma who strings it
In which Rāma strings and snaps Janaka's unyielding bow, and Janaka pledges Sītā and sends ministers to fetch Daśaratha
In which Janaka's envoys report Rāma broke the bow to win Sītā, invite Daśaratha with priests to Mithilā, and he orders march tomorrow
In which Daśaratha marches with priests, kin and fourfold army to Vidēha, where rejoicing Janaka welcomes him and fixes the wedding for morning
In which Janaka summons Kuśadhvaja and Daśaratha, and Vasiṣṭha recites the Solar lineage from Brahmā to Rāma seeking brides for Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa
In which Janaka traces his line from Nimi, tells slaying Sudhanvā, pledges Sītā to Rāma and Ūrmilā to Lakṣmaṇa, and fixes wedding day.
In which Viśvāmitra seeks Kuśadhvaja daughters for Bharata and Śatrughna, Janaka sets one wedding day and Daśaratha gives cows
In which Yudhājit visits Daśaratha, Vasiṣṭha seeks brides from ready Janaka, and four princes wed Sītā, Ūrmilā, Māṇḍavī and Śrutakīrti amid flowers and song.
In which Daśaratha marches home amid ill omens and ash-covered darkness as axe-bearing Paraśurāma appears before Rāma
In which Paraśurāma, brushing aside Daśaratha's pleading, challenges Rāma to string Viṣṇu bow and recounts its triumph over Śiva bow.
In which Rāma strings the Vaiṣṇava bow, spares brāhmaṇa Paraśurāma's life, and looses the unerring shaft on his austerity-won worlds while gods watch
In which Rāma yields his bow to Varuṇa, enters festive Ayōdhyā with brides, and dwells in deepening love with Sītā
In which Yudhājit takes Bharata and Śatrughna to Kēkaya while Rāma delights Ayōdhyā, moving old Daśaratha to crown him.
In which old Daśaratha seeks rest by naming Rāma heir, and kings with citizens praise Rāma and demand his swift crowning.
In which Daśaratha orders Vasiṣṭha and Vāmadēva toward Caitra Puṣya crowning, embraces Rāma before kings, counsels restraint, and Kausalyā and citizens rejoice.
In which Daśaratha privately warns Rāma of dreadful dreams, fixes tomorrow Puṣya crowning, and Rāma delights Kausalyā and invites Lakṣmaṇa before Sītā.
In which Daśaratha sends Vasiṣṭha to lay fast on Rāma and Sītā, while swept and flagged Ayōdhyā awaits sunrise for crowning.
In which Rāma and Sītā fast and worship Viṣṇu overnight while Ayōdhyā raises flags, lights lamps, praises Daśaratha, and fills with crowds for the crowning.
In which hunchback Mantharā sees Ayōdhyā decked for Rāma, cries danger to sleeping Kaikēyī, and Kaikēyī gifts her, seeing no slight.
In which Mantharā spurns Kaikēyī praise of Rāma, foretells slavery to Kausalyā and Bharata ruin, and urges Bharata flight to forest with kingship plotting.
In which Mantharā recalls Daśaratha's two war boons and sends jewel-stripped Kaikēyī to the anger chamber to demand Bharata crowned and Rāma exiled.
In which Daśaratha finds Kaikēyī on bare earth, swears an open boon, and hears her dreadful price of Bharata crowned and Rāma exiled fourteen years bark-clad.
In which Daśaratha pleads with pitiless Kaikēyī through the night, begs dawn never to come, and collapses senseless over Rāma exile
In which Kaikēyī cites Śaibya and Alarka on truth, threatens suicide, and sends Sumantra while Daśaratha renounces her
In which Brāhmaṇas prepare Gaṅgā water and golden vessels, miss the absent king, and Sumantra hastens to Rāma palace
In which Sumantra summons Rāma from Sītā side, and Rāma rides cheering highways toward his father with Lakṣmaṇa behind
In which Rāma crosses agaru-fumed capital through blessings, enters his father's house, and leaves citizens awaiting his return
In which Kaikēyī names her two boons, and Rāma accepts fourteen forest years, comforts his father, and turns toward departure
In which Rāma finds Kausalyā worshipping Viṣṇu for his crowning, announces fourteen forest years, and lifts his fainting mother
In which Lakṣmaṇa vows to empty Ayōdhyā with arrows, Kausalyā begs Rāma to stay, and Rāma answers with duty to father
In which Rāma orders the consecration gear withdrawn, shields Kaikēyī from blame, and lays his exile and lost crown to fate
In which Lakṣmaṇa scorns fate and offers to slay all obstructors, while Rāma wipes his tears and holds to his father word
In which Kausalyā begs to follow Rāma to the forest, and Rāma persuades her to stay and serve Daśaratha through fourteen years
In which Kausalyā performs the svastyayana blessing, invoking gods, seasons, and sages to guard Rāma in the forest
In which Rāma finds Sītā awaiting his crowning and tells her of Kaikēyī's boons, his fourteen-year exile, and her duties under Bharata
In which Sītā claims a wife shares her husband's fate and begs to walk before him into the forest rather than face heaven without him
In which Rāma paints the forest as hunger, thorns, beasts, and terrors to turn Sītā from following him
In which Sītā turns Rāma's forest terrors into virtues, cites foretold exile, and vows death by poison, fire, or water if left behind
In which Sītā shames Rāma as woman in man's form, counts thorns as cotton beside him, and wins his leave to share the exile
In which Lakṣmaṇa vows to guard Rāma and Sītā in the forest, and Rāma sends him to fetch Varuṇa's divine bows and summon Suyajña for gifts
In which Rāma honors Suyajña, rewards brāhmaṇas, servants, and dependents, and grants a cattle herd to poor gleaner Trijaṭa for a staff-cast
In which Ayōdhyā's people lament Rāma walking umbrella-less with Sītā, vow to follow him leaving empty houses to Kaikēyī, while Rāma seeks his father
In which Rāma takes leave of fainting Daśaratha, refuses the throne and a one-night delay, and yields the kingdom to Bharata
In which Daśaratha loads Rāma with army and riches, Kaikēyī cites Sagara exiling Asamañja, and the king vows to follow Rāma
In which Rāma trades royal retinue for bark garments, dresses helpless Sītā himself, and commends grieving Kausalyā to Daśaratha
In which fainting Daśaratha grants chariot and jewels, Kausalyā counsels Sītā on wifely duty, and Rāma takes leave of wailing mothers
In which Rāma, Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa mount the chariot amid wailing citizens, and ministers halt Daśaratha gazing after his speeding son
In which palace queens wail for exiled Rāma while fires die, planets menace, citizens despair, and bereft Ayōdhyā quakes
In which Daśaratha gazes till Rāma dust vanishes, renounces Kaikēyī utterly, and stumbles into Kausalyā house crying for Rāma
In which grieving Kausalyā calls Kaikēyī a freed snake, pictures the exiles on forest roots, and dreams of their showered homecoming
In which Sumitrā consoles wailing Kausalyā that righteous Rāma, soothed by sun wind and moon, will return for consecration
In which devoted citizens follow Rāma chariot, brāhmaṇas plead with Vājapēya umbrellas, and Tamasā bars his path
In which Rāma spends first night on Tamasā, praises gentle Bharata, and slips away at dawn while citizens lose his track
In which bereft city citizens curse cruel Kaikēyī, envy LakṣmaṆa and blest pools, and lament like men facing death
In which Rāma drives deep through Kōsala, hears villagers curse lust-bound father, and shows rich Kōsala to Sītā
In which Rāma halts by Gaṅgā at Śr̥ṅgavērapura where dear friend Guha offers his whole kingdom and rich nightly feast
In which wakeful LakṣmaṆa tells sorrowing sleepless Guha that old Daśaratha will soon die and widowed Ayōdhyā will fall
In which pleading Sumantra begs weeping to follow Rāma to the forest, Rāma sends him back, and exiles cross Gaṅgā
In which Rāma grieves for helpless aged Daśaratha and poor lonely Kausalyā, and LakṣmaṆa vows never to leave him
In which Bharadvāja welcomes the tired foot-worn exiles at holy Prayāga and sends them to dwell on Chitrakūṭa hill
In which Bharadvāja guides the weary exiles over the Yamunā by wooden raft to the great banyan and toward Chitrakūṭa
In which Rāma shows Sītā flowering Kiṃśuka woods and the high Chitrakūṭa peak, and LakṣmaṆa builds their leaf hut
In which Sumantra returns Rāma-less to silent Ayōdhyā, faces crowds asking for Rāma, and grieving Daśaratha faints while Kausalyā rebukes his silence
In which revived Daśaratha questions Sumantra, hears Rāma farewell to kin and Bharata, Lakṣmaṇa condemnation, and silent Sītā tears
In which Sumantra pictures mourning forest and joyless Ayōdhyā while Daśaratha confesses folly, begs for Rāma, and faints
In which trembling Kausalyā begs for Daṇḍaka while Sumantra pictures fearless Sītā at home in forest, yet she wails still
In which weeping Kausalyā pictures Sītā suffering forest hardships and warns Rāma will scorn Bharata-enjoyed kingdom as Daśaratha faints
In which rebuked Daśaratha recalls past misdeed, begs Kausalyā pardon, and grief-seized sinks to sleep as night falls
In which sleepless Daśaratha recalls youthful sound-shot sin, mistaking water pot for elephant and mortally wounding a parent-serving ascetic
In which Daśaratha confesses mistaken killing to blind parents, shows them the corpse, and receives a son-grief death curse
In which dawn attendants find lifeless Daśaratha while bedchamber women wail and awakened queens fall crying as palace mourns
In which Kausalyā curses fulfilled Kaikēyī while ministers lay Daśaratha in oil and Ayōdhyā censures Bharata mother
In which brahmanas and ministers, finding Ayodhya kingless after Dasharatha death and Rama exile, urge Vasishtha to consecrate a prince
In which Vasishtha sends swift messengers to Rajagriha, bidding Bharata hasten home while concealing his father death and Rama exile
In which Bharata, while messengers enter Rajagriha, dreams his father falling into dung, drinking oil, and riding south toward death
In which Bharata, hearing urgent yet evasive summons, takes leave of his grandfather and hastens toward Ayodhya with Shatrughna
In which Bharata speeds across rivers and forests for seven nights, then finds Ayodhya silent, dusty, joyless, and full of evil omens
In which Kaikeyi tells grieving Bharata his father died and Rama walks in Dandaka, then urges him to take the throne
In which Bharata calls Kaikeyi his family death-night, rejects her stolen throne, and vows to bring Rama back from exile
In which Bharata curses Kaikeyi as a demoness, tells of Surabhi weeping for burdened oxen, and vows to fetch Rama
In which Kausalya accuses Bharata of gaining a thornless throne, and Bharata swears dreadful oaths denying any part in Rama exile
In which Vasishtha steadies Bharata, priests bear Dasharatha on a bier to sandal pyre, and mourners offer Sarayu water
In which Bharata performs śrāddha gifts, wails at his father ash-covered pyre with Śatrughna, and Vasiṣṭha and Sumantra console the fallen brothers
In which wrathful Śatrughna seizes adorned Mantharā, drags her wailing and reviles Kaikēyī until Bharata forbids killing women
In which ministers offer leaderless throne to Bharata, who refuses for elder Rāma, vows forest life, and orders a road to fetch him
In which skilled workmen clear forests, level ground, dig tanks and wells, and raise moated camps as the highway reaches the Gaṅgā
In which awakened Bharata disclaims kingship and mourns rudderless Lakṣmī while Vasiṣṭha convenes the golden assembly to hail him
In which Vasiṣṭha urges Bharata to take the throne, tearful Bharata declares Rāma alone king, and musters the army to fetch him
In which Bharata leads a vast army with mothers citizens and artisans to the Gaṅgā, camps overnight, and offers water for his father
In which Guha rallies fishermen guards fearing Bharata comes to kill Rāma, then brings fish meat honey and offers lodging
In which Bharata swears he comes only to fetch fatherlike Rāma, Guha praises his renunciation, and night grief burns him sleepless
In which Guha recounts sleepless Lakṣmaṇa refusing a bed, foretelling a widowed earth, and guarding Rāma till dawn ferry crossing
In which Bharata faints at Guha tidings, mourning mothers gather, and Guha recounts Rāma refusing food and sleeping beneath an iṅgudī tree
In which Bharata beholds Rāma trampled grass bed, laments palace bred Rāma on hard earth, and vows ground sleep should Rāma refuse return
In which Bharata wakes at dawn, summons Guha and five hundred boats, ferries the whole army with swimming elephants, and sets out for Prayāga forest
In which Bharata approaches Bharadvāja on foot with Vasiṣṭha, tearfully denies coveting Rāma kingdom, and learns his brother waits at Citrakūṭa
In which Bharadvāja invokes Viśvakarman and summons palaces, pāyasa rivers, Gandharvas, and serving women to feast wondering Bharata army overnight
In which Bharadvāja directs Bharata to Mandākinī and Citrakūṭa, greets his grieving mothers, absolves Kaikēyī, and watches the army march south
In which Bharata marvels at flowering Citrakūṭa alive with deer and Kiṃnaras, halts his army at rising smoke, and proceeds with Sumantra and preceptor toward Rāma
In which Rāma consoles Sītā with mineral bright peaks, teeming beasts, flowering groves, waterfalls, and lover beds surpassing northern Kurus
In which Rāma displays the swan haunted Mandākinī to moon faced Sītā and bids her bathe, play, and love mountain and river as home
In which Rāma hears army dust and fleeing herds, Lakṣmaṇa spies Kōvidāra bannered Bharata from a śāla tree, and rages to slaughter the invaders
In which Rāma soothes Lakṣmaṇa's rage at Bharata's host, trusts his brother's love, and sees the army camp gently by the hill
In which Bharata, leaving his army behind, searches the woods on foot and rejoices to see Rāma's fire-banner smoke
In which Bharata finds Rāma's humble leaf hut, grieves his brother's ascetic guise, and collapses weeping at his feet
In which Rāma embraces Bharata and quizzes him closely on the king, ministers, spies, treasury, justice, and guarded Ayodhyā
In which Bharata tells of Daśaratha's death, Rāma swoons, and the brothers offer water and wild cakes to their father
In which the queens mourn Rāma's wild offerings and exile garb, embrace Sītā, and watch Rāma honor Vasiṣṭha beside Bharata
In which Bharata pleads for Rāma's crowning, and Rāma, absolving his brother, insists each must keep their father's separate command
In which Bharata presses the crown with parables, Rāma answers with mortality and duty, and Bharata vows to follow him to the woods
In which Rāma cites Kaikeyī's two boons and Gayā's verse on sons, keeping the forest for himself and giving the throne to Bharata
In which Jābāli, consoling Bharata, tempts Rāma with unbelief, calling kinship, śrāddha, and heaven delusions to seize the throne
In which Rāma refutes Jābāli counsel, praises truth as dharma and heaven root, and vows to keep his father forest promise
In which Vasiṣṭha soothes angry Rāma, recounts creation and Solar kings to Daśaratha, and asks Rāma to take the throne
In which Vasiṣṭha cites three gurus, Bharata vows fasting before Rāma, and Rāma refuses while Bharata offers to live fourteen years in forest
In which hidden seers bless the brothers, Bharata pleads for Rāma to take the kingdom, and Rāma gives his sandals and sends all home
In which Bharata carries the sandals, reports Rāma fourteen year vow to Bharadvāja, and returns to descry desolate Ayōdhyā
In which Bharata enters desolate Ayōdhyā likened to dark night and spent altar, and asks his charioteer why song and scent are gone
In which Bharata vows to wait at Nandigrāma, installs the sandals as trust, and governs clad in bark until Rāma returns
In which Rāma questions the agitated ascetics, hears Khara fiends befoul fires and vessels, and sees Kulapati depart for the old āśrama
In which Rāma leaves trampled Citrakūṭa, receives sonlike welcome at Atri āśrama, and sends Sītā to Anasūyā, maker of roots, fruits, and Gaṅgā, who teaches husband devotion
In which Sītā affirms husband devotion, receives unfading garland, dress, ornaments, and unguent from Anasūyā, then recounts furrow birth, bow, and wedding
In which Anasūyā embraces adorned Sītā at nightfall, Rāma rejoices at her divine gifts, and ascetics show the demon-beset forest path
In which Rama enters Dandakaranya, wondering sages welcome and feast him, then teach that a revenue-taking king must shelter ascetics.
In which the man-eating Viradha snatches Sita for his wife, Rama laments Kaikeyi's triumph, and Lakshmana vows his arrow will fell Viradha.
In which Rama maims spear-hurling Viradha, the fallen foe confesses cursed Tumburu freed by Rama's blows, and burial wins him heaven.
In which Indra in his sky-chariot courts Sharabhanga heavenward, the sage waits to see Rama, then sheds his body in fire for Brahmaloka.
In which gathered ascetics show Rama slaughtered bodies, plead that a sixth-share king must guard them, and Rama vows slaughter before seeking Sutikshna.
In which awaiting Sutikshna embraces Rama, offers his heaven-won worlds for Rama's household stay, and Rama refuses long lodging to spare the trusting deer.
In which Rama worships at dawn, embraces farewell with Sutikshna, views lotus lakes and peacock woods, and Sita arms both brothers for the road.
In which Sita pleads against vow-driven slaughter of Dandaka rakshasas, citing the ascetic whose entrusted sword bred cruelty and dragged him to hell.
In which Rama answers Sita that pity-seeking sages won his sworn word, truth forbids recall, and pledged brahmanas outweigh life itself.
In which Rama marvels at five-apsara music, dwells ten years touring hermitages, hears Vatapi digested and Ilvala burnt, and nears Agastya bidding Lakshmana announce him.

In which Rāvaṇa brands Vibhīṣaṇa kin-traitor for wholesome plea, and Vibhīṣaṇa soars with four comrades refusing to watch Rāma arrows kill his brother

In which Rama vows never to abandon a friend-comer, recalls dove and Kandu law of refuge, and grants Vibhishana fearlessness
In which Rama crowns surrendered Vibhishana as Lanka king, asks how to cross the ocean, and lies on kusha grass awaiting reply
In which the ocean scorns three nights of worship, and wrathful Rama strings his bow to dry its waters with fiery shafts
In which the ocean offers Nala as bridge-builder, monkeys fill the sea with trees and rocks, and gods bless Rama crossing

In which Sarana names bear lord Dhumra, wise Jambavan, Kesari, Shatabali and countless mountain-bodied hosts thirsting for Lanka
In which Shuka points to Mainda, Dvivida, sun-snatching Hanuman, Rama, Lakshmana, Vibhishana and garlanded Sugriva craving battle
In which Ravana banishes enemy-praising spies, sends new watchers to learn Rama habits, and hears the mauled survivors tell of Suvela
In which Śārdūla, beaten by monkeys and spared by Rāma, names the monkey chiefs while Rāvaṇa refuses to yield Sītā
In which Rāvaṇa stages a sorcerer's false head and bow to convince grieving Sītā that Rāma and his host lie slain
In which Sītā wails over the seeming head of Rāma and seeks death, till war business calls Rāvaṇa away
In which kindly Saramā unmasks the false head and heartens Sītā with Rāma's camp and coming rescue
In which Saramā spies on Rāvaṇa and brings Sītā word of his fixed resolve and Rāma's destined vengeance
In which aged Mālyavān reads the bloody omens and begs Rāvaṇa to render Sītā and seek peace
In which Rāvaṇa spurns Mālyavān's counsel, swears never to bend, and mans Laṅkā gates for war
In which spies map Laṅkā gates and Rāma arrays Nīla and Aṅgada and Hanumān for assault
In which Rāma climbs Suvēla with his host, sights Laṅkā aloft, and rests under moonlight before battle
In which the host sports through Laṅkā groves while Rāma gazes on golden gated Trikūṭa crowned city
In which Rāma marks dread omens, besieges Laṅkā gate by gate, and sends Aṅgada who delivers his ultimatum and shatters Rāvaṇa palace tower
In which Rāvaṇa beholds Laṅkā girt by countless monkeys, orders his armies out, and godlike slaughter rages on the ramparts
In which champions meet in single combats, Aṅgada wrecks Indrajit, Rāma beheads four, and monkeys mangle the night-roaming foe
In which night confuses friend and foe, Rāma clears the quarters with arrows, and vanished Indrajit rains unseen shafts
In which hidden Indrajit eludes sky-searching monkeys, binds Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa with snake arrows, and fells them senseless
In which exulting Indrajit claims Rāma dead before Laṅkā, and Vibhīṣaṇa checks Sugrīva despair and rallies the scattered host
In which Rāvaṇa sets Sītā in Puṣpaka to behold fallen Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, and she deems her husband dead
In which Sītā counts her blissful marks false over fallen Rāma, and Trijaṭā proves the brothers live and brings her home
In which reviving Rāma mourns Lakṣmaṇa as dead, vows to follow him, and bids Sugrīva bear the host home
In which Vibhīṣaṇa laments and Suṣeṇa seeks herbs, till Garuḍa scatters the snakes, heals the brothers, and monkeys rally
In which Rāvaṇa learns Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa escaped the arrow bond and hurls Dhūmrākṣa west past bleeding omens toward Hanumān
In which monkeys and demons trade trees for arrows while Hanumān wrecks Dhūmrākṣa chariot and splits his skull
In which Rāvaṇa looses Akampana past evil omens into dust blinded slaughter where Kumuda and Nala storm the vanguard
In which Akampana scatters the monkeys until Hanumān breaks his mountain and brains him with a tree
In which Rāvaṇa vows no escape but war, Prahasta pledges his life, and rolls east amid jackals and falling goads
In which monkey chiefs behead Prahasta ministers before Nīla wrecks his horses and splits his head with rock
In which Rāvaṇa fells Sugrīva and Nīla and Lakṣmaṇa until Rāma rides Hanumān, strips his chariot and crown, and lets him live
In which beaten Rāvaṇa recalls Brahmā warning and rouses snoring Kumbhakarṇa with meat mountains and thousand drums
In which Vibhīṣaṇa tells how Brahmā doomed devouring Kumbhakarṇa to sleep while Nīla bars the gates with boulders
In which Kumbhakarṇa strides flower strewn to Rāvaṇa palace to find him begging rescue from Rāma bridge crossed host
In which laughing Kumbhakarṇa lectures grieving Rāvaṇa on forethought and statecraft, endures sharp rebuke, and vows to slay Rāma and scatter the monkey host
In which Mahōdara scolds boastful Kumbhakarṇa, praises Rāvaṇa wisdom, and plots to win despairing Sītā by false news of Rāma death
In which scorned Kumbhakarṇa rebukes Mahōdara, takes blazing spear with Rāvaṇa blessings, swells mountainlike despite dire omens, and marches roaring from Laṅkā to scatter the monkey host
In which steadfast Aṅgada shames fleeing monkeys, leads rock and tree assault on Kumbhakarṇa, and rallies the chiefs to stand
In which Hanumān and five chiefs fall before Kumbhakarṇa, Sugrīva is seized and bites free, and Rāma at last severs his arms feet and head
In which Rāvaṇa mourns fallen Kumbhakarṇa, recalls spurned Vibhīṣaṇa counsel, and sinks in grief
In which Triśiras rebukes grieving Rāvaṇa, marches with four sons and two uncles to battle, and Aṅgada slays Narāntaka in duel
In which Dēvāntaka Mahōdara and Triśiras beset Aṅgada, and Hanumān Nīla and R̥ṣabha slay Dēvāntaka Mahōdara Triśiras and Mahāpārśva
In which giant Atikāya terrifies the monkeys, scorns boy Lakṣmaṇa, and falls to his Brāhma arrow after Vāyu counsel
In which Indrajit consoles mourning Rāvaṇa, wins fire with Nikumbhilā rites, and fells unseen Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa with Brāhma shafts
In which Vibhīṣaṇa steadies routed monkeys, Jāmbavān sends Hanumān to Himālaya for four herbs, and fallen hosts rise healed
In which Sugrīva sends torch monkeys to burn Laṅkā while Rāvaṇa looses Kumbha and Nikumbha into roaring night battle
In which Aṅgada brains Kampana with a peak while Sugrīva breaks Kumbha bow and fells him with a vajra fist
In which Nikumbha whirls his blazing parigha until Hanumān breaks free, crushes him, and twists off his head
In which Rāvaṇa sends Khara son Makarākṣa to kill Rāma, and Makarākṣa rolls out boasting amid falling banners and stumbling horses
In which Makarākṣa demands duel for slain father Khara until Rāma cuts his bow, spear and burns his heart with fire
In which Indrajit feeds fire, vanishes in a charmed car, and bloodies Rāma Lakṣmaṇa while Rāma checks Lakṣmaṇa Brāhma vow
In which Indrajit sets weeping false Sītā on his car and swords her before Hanumān, who breaks in grief
In which Hanumān rallies runners, misses Indrajit with a rock, and withdraws to tell Rāma while fire drinks blood
In which Hanumān tells Rāma of Sītā death, Rāma falls senseless, and Lakṣmaṇa scorns dharma and vows burning Laṅkā
In which Vibhīṣaṇa finds Rāma senseless over false Sītā slaughter and urges sending Lakṣmaṇa before Nikumbhilā rite succeeds
In which Rāma accepts Vibhīṣaṇa counsel and sends armed Lakṣmaṇa with monkey bears to stop Indrajit at Nikumbhilā
In which Lakṣmaṇa storms the demon screen while Hanumān challenges Indrajit and Vibhīṣaṇa marks the Vāsava conqueror for death
In which Vibhīṣaṇa shows the Nyagrōdha that makes Indrajit invisible and answers traitor taunts with Rāvaṇa faults
In which boastful Indrajit on his black horse car trades venom shafts and taunts with unboastful Lakṣmaṇa
In which Lakṣmaṇa strips Indrajit armor while both bleed tirelessly until Vibhīṣaṇa steps to aid him
In which Vibhīṣaṇa rallies monkeys over fallen chiefs while Lakṣmaṇa unhorses Indrajit and monkeys crush his car
In which Lakṣmaṇa answers Yama Kubēra and Raudra shafts with Varuṇa and severs Indrajit with truth sworn Indra dart
In which bloodied Lakṣmaṇa brings severed head news while Rāma embraces him and Suṣēṇa herb heals all
In which son-bereaved Rāvaṇa rushes sword at Sītā in Aśōka while she mourns Rāma Lakṣmaṇa Kausalyā until Supārśva restrains him
In which Ravana sends his generals against Rama, whose Gandharva weapon multiplies him thousandfold while demons kill their own doubles.
In which grieving rakshasa widows blame Shurpanakha, list Rama past victories, and foresee Sita devouring Lanka with Ravana.
In which Ravana, stung by widows wailing, vows revenge, ignores dire omens, and rides out to crush Rama and monkeys.
In which Sugriva stops the rout, exchanges tree, rock, sword, and fist with Virupaksha, and fells him with a temple blow.
In which Sugriva meets Mahodara, Ravana last hope, breaks mace, musala, and swords, and severs his helmeted head.
In which Angada answers Mahaparshva arrow storm with whirling parigha and palm, then bursts his heart with a paternal fist.
In which Ravana fells Rama tree vowing revenge, burns monkeys with darkness, and duels Rama through serpent and fire arrows.
In which Ravana, stripped of chariot and driver, spears Lakshmana through the chest, and Rama swears the world shall hold Rama or Ravana alone.
In which Rama despairs over fallen Lakshmana, Sushena sends Hanuman for herbs, and the revived brother demands Ravana death before sunset.
In which gods send Indra chariot to even the duel, and Rama answers Ravana serpent arrows with swooping golden eagles.
In which enraged Rāma shatters Rāvaṇa's hurled pike with Indra's javelin and leaves the demon king bleeding like flowering aśōka
In which Rāma denounces Rāvaṇa for stealing Sītā like a thief and batters him senseless until his charioteer bears him away
In which Rāvaṇa accuses his charioteer of cowardice, hears his loyal plea for rest, and speeds back to face Rāma
In which Rāma circles to meet Rāvaṇa's chariot as dreadful omens beset Rāvaṇa and bright victory signs hearten Rāma
In which both armies watch spellbound as Rāma fells Rāvaṇa's banner and both fill the sky with arrows
In which Rāma lops a hundred new heads from Rāvaṇa in vain and puzzles over his dulled arrows as battle burns ceaselessly
In which Mātali prompts Rāma to loose Brahmā's world-fire arrow through Rāvaṇa's heart amid drums and flower rain
In which Rāvaṇa's queens rush wailing to the field, clasp his corpse, and blame his scorned counsel and stolen Sītā
In which Mandōdarī mourns Rāvaṇa as Sītā's victim while Rāma bids reluctant Vibhīṣaṇa honor him with funeral fire
In which Rāma dismisses Indra's chariot, crowns Vibhīṣaṇa king of Laṅkā, and sends Hanumān to bear Sītā the victory tidings
In which Hanuman announces Rama victory to joyful speechless Sita, seeks leave to crush cruel rakshasis, and learns forgiveness from her old verse on compassion
In which Rama orders bathed Sita brought in state, rebukes Vibhishana for driving away his own people, and receives veiled weeping Sita before wondering friends
In which Rama claims victory for manliness not Sita, rejects Ravana-touched Sita as intolerable to his lineage, and leaves her trembling like a creeper struck by an elephant trunk
In which Sita answers Rama harsh words with an oath of chaste heart, asks why she was not abandoned at Hanuman message, and walks into blazing fire before grieving crowds
In which gods led by Brahma question Rama overlooking Sita in fire, hear his human claim, and reveal him as Narayana Vishnu whose task of Ravana slaying is done
In which Fire returns pure Sita untouched even in mind, and Rama declares his harsh test meant to vindicate her before the three worlds as shore bounds ocean
In which Maheshvara sends Rama to Bharata and kingdom, and father Dasharatha descends to embrace his sons lift Kaikeyi curse and instruct Lakshmana and Sita
In which Rama asks Indra to revive selfless monkeys woundless with unseasonal plenty, and the gods praise him then send him to Ayodhya Bharata and consecration
In which Rama refuses Vibhishana bath feast and garments without Bharata, chooses swift Ayodhya return, and receives the described divine Pushpaka seized from Kubera
In which Rama rewards monkeys honours allies and bids farewell to Kishkindha and Lanka, then yields to their wish to see Ayodhya anointing and boards all in sky-rising Pushpaka
In which Rāma, soaring home in Puṣpaka, points out Laṅkā, the sea bridge, Kiṣkindhā and exile landmarks to Sītā above brightening Ayōdhyā.
In which Bharadvāja, knowing Rāma exile war and return by tapas, hosts him overnight and ripens the Ayōdhyā road trees.
In which Rāma dispatches Hanumān to probe Bharata mind and Hanumān greets Guha before finding bark-clad Bharata awaiting him.
In which Hanumān, asked how Rāma met monkeys, recounts exile, abduction, leap, war and Puṣpaka return before tomorrow meeting.
In which Bharata decks the road, welcomes Puṣpaka-borne Rāma with kin and city, takes back pādukās and sees the vimāna released.
In which Bharata returns the burden, Rāma is anointed with Sītā, honors vānaras and Hanumān, and establishes a disease-free golden reign.
In which sages hail Rāma for slaying Rāvaṇa and his host, marvel above all at fallen Indrajit, and Rāma asks how Indra was conquered.
In which Pulastya curses sporting maidens with pregnancy, weds Tr̥ṇabindu daughter, and fathers Viśravas, forefather of Rāvaṇa line.
In which Viśravas son Vaiśravaṇa gains riches lordship and Puṣpaka through penance and settles forsaken Laṅkā at father bidding.
In which Brahmā word spawns Rākṣasas and Yakṣas, Hēti line bears forsaken Sukēśa, and Śiva grants him ageless life and sky city with Umā speeding births.
In which Sukēśa three sons gain Brahmā boons, settle golden Laṅkā built by Viśvakarman, and wed the three Narmadā maidens.
In which gods seek refuge from Mālyavān horde, Viṣṇu vows their slaughter, and the Rākṣasa army marches heavenward through bleeding skies.
In which Viṣṇu breaks the night-roamer host with arrows and conch, fells Mālin with the sunlike discus, and drives the remnant fleeing to Laṅkā.
In which Mālyavān braves Viṣṇu spear to spear, Garuḍa wing sweeps him off, and the broken host forsakes Laṅkā for Pātāla before Nārāyaṇa-born Rāma.
In which Sumālin weds Kaikasī to Viśravas at a dread hour, she bears ten-headed Rāvaṇa with giant and righteous brothers, and jealousy drives him to penance.
In which Rāvaṇa buys immunity with nine severed heads, Vibhīṣaṇa chooses steadfast dharma and life, and Sarasvatī turns Kumbhakarṇa tongue to endless sleep.
In which Sumālin rises from Rasātala to claim Laṅkā, Prahasta preaches heroic brotherlessness, and Kubēra cedes the city as Rāvaṇa takes consecration.
In which Rāvaṇa bestows Śūrpaṇakhā on Vidyujjihva, weds Mandōdarī by fire, settles his brothers, and hails newborn Mēghanāda.
In which Kumbhakarṇa claims a vast sleeping palace, Kubēra warns Rāvaṇa through an envoy, and Rāvaṇa kills the messenger and marches to conquest.
In which Rāvaṇa marches on Kailāsa with six ministers, routs the Yakṣa host, and batters down the gate guardian to force entrance.
In which Kubēra reproaches Rāvaṇa, trades mace strokes and fire-water missiles, and loses Puṣpaka to his brother conqueror.
In which Puṣpaka stalls beneath Śiva, monkey-faced Nandī foretells monkey ruin, and Śiva crushes Rāvaṇa lifting arms and names him Rāvaṇa.
In which Rāvaṇa lusts for ascetic Vēdavatī, touches her hair, and watches her enter fire to be reborn as Sītā for his ruin.
In which Rāvaṇa finds Marutta ringed by gods turned to birds and beasts, eats the sages, and gods repay their hosts with shining boons.
In which great kings yield to Rāvaṇa, Anaraṇya of Ayōdhyā fights alone, and dying foretells an Ikṣvāku king who will kill Rāvaṇa.
In which Nārada hails Rāvaṇa amid mortal joy and grief, points him to Yama city, and follows wondering how Death itself can be beaten.
In which Narada warns Yama of Ravana, who frees hell sufferers, batters guards, burns the host with Pashupata and roars across the earth
In which Yama fights Ravana seven nights, lifts the infallible Time staff, heeds Brahma and vanishes while Ravana claims victory.
In which Ravana makes friends of Nivatakavachas, kills Kalakeyas, storms Varuna palace and routs his sons in sky combat.
In which Ravana drags captive maidens to Lanka, suffers chaste curse of woman-caused death and settles widowed Shurpanakha with Khara in Dandaka.
In which Ravana finds Meghanada crowned with Shiva boons, hears Madhu stole Kumbhinasi, marches to Madhupura and spares him for heaven campaign.
In which Ravana halts Rambha on Kailasa, assaults his pleading daughter-in-law by force and earns Nalakubara curse of bursting head.
In which Indra begs Vishnu for aid, Vishnu vows Ravana death, and Vasu Savitra slays Sumali as gods and rakshasas clash.
In which Meghanada routs Jayanta, Puloma bears him to ocean, Kumbhakarna rages, and Indra duels Ravana in darkness.
In which Ravana storms encircled through dark, Indra seeks capture, and unseen Meghanada binds Indra with maya and ends the battle.
In which Brahma crowns Meghanada Indrajit, buys Indra with rite-bound boon, and traces defeat to Ahalya assault and Gautama curse.
In which Rāvaṇa, missing Arjuna at Māhiṣmatī, boasts that sun wind and river fear him and worships Śiva on the Narmadā bank
In which Arjuna dams the Narmadā with a thousand arms, floods Rāvaṇa rite, and binds dazed Rāvaṇa like Bali
In which Pulastya flies to Māhiṣmatī, begs Arjuna to release grandson Rāvaṇa, and joins them in fire-witnessed friendship
In which Rāvaṇa creeps to seize praying Vālin, is carried armpit-tucked around four oceans, and sues for brotherhood
In which Rāma hails Hanumān above Vālin and Rāvaṇa and asks Agastya why he spared Vālin and forgot his strength
In which Brahmā revives the bolt-struck child, gods grant him immunity and long life, and sages curse him to forget his strength
In which Rāma embraces friend Pratardana, sends him to Vārāṇasī, and dismisses allied kings with praise and leave
In which boastful kings depart with gifts, Rāma shares them among monkeys and Rākṣasas, and all feast two happy months
In which Rāma sends Sugrīva and Vibhīṣaṇa to rule righteously and grants Hanumān life while his story endures
In which Puṣpaka returns from Kubēra for Rāma service, is worshipped and freed, and Bharata reports golden age wonders
In which Rāma feasts with Sītā in the blossoming Aśōka grove and grants her wish to visit the Gaṅgā hermitages.
In which Rāma demands the talk of city and country and learns men mock him for keeping Sītā after her captivity.
In which Rāma summons Lakṣmaṇa, Bharata, and Śatrughna and tearfully begs their counsel in his trouble.
In which Rāma, stung by city-country slander against sinless Sītā, commands Lakṣmaṇa to abandon her beyond the Gaṅgā.
In which Lakṣmaṇa carries eager Sītā toward the Gaṅgā while she notes dark omens and prays for all Ayōdhyā.
In which Lakṣmaṇa crosses Sītā over the Gaṅgā and tells her Rāma casts her off, sinless, for fear of scandal.
In which Sītā swoons at her casting off, sends Rāma a message of duty, and is left weeping in the echoing forest.
In which Vālmīki hastens to wailing Sītā on the Gaṅgā bank and settles her among his sheltering ascetic women.
In which Lakṣmaṇa bewails Sītā banishment on the road while Sumantra recalls old brahmin warnings of coming partings.
In which Sumantra tells how Durvāsas foretold Rāma long reign, kin partings, and ascent to Brahmalōka after many sacrifices.
In which Lakṣmaṇa reenters Ayōdhyā fearing Rāma, finds him tearful on throne, reports abandoning Sītā, and soothes him toward firmness
In which more than a hundred Yamunā sages enter palace with holy water, praise Rāma, and seek promised rescue from terror
In which Cyavana recounts Madhu winning Śiva spear, bequeathing it to wicked Lavaṇa, who now torments three worlds and sages
In which Rāma questions sages about Lavaṇa, promises death, grants eager Śatrughna the task, and orders him consecrated for Madhu kingdom
In which Śatrughna bows to Rāma command, gains consecration and primordial arrow, and learns to challenge Lavaṇa before he grasps Śiva spear
In which Rāma equips Śatrughna with army wealth and secret march plan, fixes rainy season death, and sends him bowing toward Madhu forest
In which Śatrughna halts at Vālmīki āśrama, accepts welcome hospitality, and hears Saudāsa cursed for serving human flesh to Vasiṣṭha
In which Sītā delivers twin boys at midnight, Vālmīki protects and names them Kuśa Lava, and joyful Śatrughna proceeds toward Yamunā
In which Cyavana tells how Lavaṇa spear burned Māndhātr̥ and his host, proving spear strength, yet promises Śatrughna victory at dawn
In which Śatrughna blocks Madhu gate bow in hand, trades insults with prey laden Lavaṇa, and refuses leave to fetch his weapon
In which Śatrughna trades taunts with Lavaṇa, endures hurled trees and swooning fall, and fells him with Viṣṇu's world-feared arrow as Brahmā and gods watch.
In which gods offer Śatrughna a boon for killing Lavaṇa, he chooses fair Madhupurī, and builds thriving Śūrasēnā on the Yamunā in twelve years.
In which Śatrughna journeys to Ayōdhyā, tells Rāma of Lavaṇa's death and new Mathurā, and stays five nights before returning.
In which an aged brāhmaṇa bears his dead child to the palace gate, wails his sinless loss, and charges Rāma's fault for untimely death.
In which Rāma gathers eight sages, Nārada traces yuga dharma from Kr̥ta to Dvāpara, and blames a śūdra ascetic for the child's death.
In which Rāma seals the dead boy in oil, patrols west north east and south in Puṣpaka, and questions a downward-hanging tapasvin by a lake.
In which Śambūka seeks heaven in body through tapas, Rāma severs his head reviving the boy, and Agastya offers a Viśvakarman jewel.
In which Agastya recalls entering a beastless forest, watching a shining vimāna descend, and questioning a corpse-eating heaven-dweller by the lake.
In which Śvēta recounts ruling Vidēha, starving in Brahmalōka for never giving, eating his own flesh, and trading a jewel for release.
In which Rāma asks why Śvēta's wood lacked beasts and men, and Agastya tells Manu counseling Ikṣvāku and banishing dull Daṇḍa southward.
In which King Daṇḍa lusts for sage Bhārgava's daughter Arajā, ignores her plea to woo her father, and ravishes her by force
In which wrathful Bhārgava curses Daṇḍa to death in seven nights, dooms his realm to dust rain, and shelters Arajā by the lake
In which Rāma keeps evening rites with Agastya, receives his praise as world purifier, and flies Puṣpaka home to Ayōdhyā
In which Rāma proposes the Rājasūya rite with his brothers, and Bharata persuades him that guarding subjects equals sacrifice
In which Lakṣmaṇa commends the cleansing Aśvamēdha and tells how righteous Vr̥tra tapas drove fearful Indra to Viṣṇu
In which Viṣṇu divides himself threefold so Indra can strike Vr̥tra, then promises the stained god cleansing through horse sacrifice
In which gods perform the Aśvamēdha for hiding Indra, lodge his brahmahatyā fourfold, and restore the withered world
In which hunting King Ila strays into Śiva's woman-formed grove, turns female with his retinue, and wins alternating sexes
In which woman-formed Ilā sports through forest to Budha lake, stirs its waters, and Budha settles her followers as Kiṃpuruṣīs
In which Budha loves woman-formed Ilā for a month, detains man-restored Ila a year, and receives newborn Purūravas
In which Rāma tells how Ila, turned woman, regains manhood through a Śiva horse sacrifice and founds Pratiṣṭhāna.
In which Rāma vows a horse sacrifice, summons priests, and invites monkeys, rākṣasas, kings, and sages to Naimiṣa on the Gōmatī.
In which Rāma frees the horse for his Naimiṣa sacrifice while monkeys and rākṣasas serve sages and shower beggars with gifts.
In which Vālmīki settles near the sacrifice ground and bids his two pupils sing the Rāmāyaṇa daily before Rāma and the priests.
In which two forest boys enchant Rāma with twenty sargas, refuse his gold, and reveal Vālmīki five-hundred-sarga epic of his life.
In which Rāma, knowing the singers as Sītā sons, seeks her public oath through Vālmīki and summons all to witness it tomorrow.
In which Vālmīki brings tearful Sītā before kings, sages, monkeys, and rākṣasas, vouching her purity and naming her twins Rāma sons.
In which Rāma trusts Vālmīki word, and Sītā, swearing sole love for Rāma, sinks with Earth goddess into Rasātala amid divine flowers.
In which Rāma, deeming the world empty without Sītā, rules Ayōdhyā with a golden image, sacrifices for ages, and mourns his mothers.
In which Yudhājit envoy offers Gandharva land on the Sindhu, and Rāma sends Bharata with Takṣa and Puṣkala to conquer and found two cities.
In which Bharata battles Gandharvas seven nights, looses the Saṃvarta weapon, founds two splendid cities, and returns to Rāma.
In which Rāma seeks a faultless realm for Aṅgada and Candrakētu, builds Aṅgadīyā and Candrakāntā, and crowns both princes.
In which Kāla as a blazing ascetic seeks Rāma as Atibala messenger and demands death-guarded private talk.
In which Kāla declares Rāma Viṣṇu born to slay Rāvaṇa, announces his completed years, and summons him heavenward.
In which Durvāsas demands instant audience under curse threat, Lakṣmaṇa interrupts Rāma, and Rāma serves desired food.
In which Lakṣmaṇa offers death for broken guarded talk, Vasiṣṭha bids renunciation, and Lakṣmaṇa ascends embodied to heaven.
In which Rāma names Bharata king and seeks forest death, Bharata refuses, and Rāma crowns Kuśa and Lava.
In which messengers report Rāma resolve, Śatrughna crowns two sons in Mathurā and Vaidīśa, rushes to Ayōdhyā, and vanaras seek to follow.
In which Rāma walks silent in linen with Śrī Hrī and Vēdas, and wives, priests, citizens and monkeys follow heavenward.
In which Brahmā welcomes Rāma at Sarayū, Rāma resumes Viṣṇu form, and gods grant followers Sāntānika and Brahmalōka abodes.
